name: PT Astra International Tbk

frontmatter.title: Astra International: book floors for the unlisted parts, a discount the market has nearly matched, and an ADD
frontmatter.summary: Revision answers eleven red-team challenges: infrastructure moves to the book value of its stakes, property to a market-anchored asset mark, financing to a normalised return on an improving credit trend, and the cost path to the audited ratio. The market now implies a discount narrower than our base, inside the card range, so the base value sits below the price and the return is the cost-of-equity roll plus the dividend. Target Rp5,162, expected return 11.2%: ADD.
thesis: The parts are worth Rp4,834 per share after a 30% discount taken from the method card's range, not from the share price; the discount is the base rate and the target is an output [S0, S15, S21, S22, S23, S27].

The unlisted blocks now sit on floors we can source: infrastructure at the book value of its own stakes, property on the listed subsidiary's market value applied to the group's asset base, and financing on a normalised return that the credit trend supports [S15, S27, S26].
The market price implies 27.6%, inside the card's range and near its midpoint, so the expected return is the cost-of-equity roll plus the dividend rather than a discount recovery [S0, S15].

The automotive block and the earnings model now use one run-rate: the third-quarter exit in the mark, and a fourth quarter within a twentieth of the third quarter's clean pace once the non-recurring charge is handled on the same basis [S14, S15, S20].

The tails are discount-path probabilities, disclosed as narrower than a true operating set; the operating breaks the engine cannot reprice are quantified in the text rather than left implicit [S15, S14, S26].

catalysts.event: Astra voluntary tender offer for Astra Otoparts closes
FY2026 audited results, final dividend and buyback-execution disclosure

frontmatter.catalyst_note: No dated discount-narrowing catalyst exists. The buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM is authorised and ongoing with no disclosed end date or pace [S8, S14, S16]; the dated capital-allocation event is the Otoparts tender close, which lifts an already consolidated stake rather than upstreaming value to the holdco [S13, S14].

blocks.text: **What changed.** This revision answers the red team's eleven challenges and moves four marks, one cost path and the scenario labelling. The Infrastructure and Logistics block moves from an own-history earnings multiple to the book value of the segment's own equity stakes, IDR22.68tn at 30 September 2026 [S15, F123]; the prior mark was about four-tenths of that book, and the block is no longer called small without a reconciliation. The Property block moves from a residual behind the listed subsidiary's earnings to an asset mark anchored on Mega Manunggal's own market value: MMLP closed at Rp214 on 6 November 2026 [S27, F119], which values its IDR6.48tn of assets at a fraction of book, and the same ratio applied to Menara Astra's IDR26.48tn of consolidated assets gives a mark several times the prior residual. The financing block's return is normalised to the annualised actual rather than haircut, because Adira's own nine-month release shows provisions falling and the non-performing ratio improving [S26, F128, F129]. The cost path glides from the nine-month ratio to the audited FY2025 ratio instead of holding a permanent step-up [S15, S6]. The discount stays at the card midpoint, but the market-implied discount has moved to 27.6%, inside the range and near the midpoint, which is the substantive change to the variant view.

**The call.** Target Rp5,162 against Rp5,000, an expected total return of 11.2% including Rp399 of dividends: **ADD**. The base path is Rp5,198; the bear Rp4,486 at 30% and the bull Rp5,907 at 25%. The target sits above the price because the base compounds at the cost of equity and nets the dividend, not because the price is cheap against our marks: the 27.6% discount the price implies is narrower than the 30% we hold, so the base sum of the parts of Rp4,834 sits below the Rp5,000 price and the return is the roll plus the dividend.

**Variant view.** The market capitalises the parts at a 27.6% discount, which is inside the method card's persistent range and close to its midpoint. Our base holds 30% because no dated narrowing catalyst exists — the only named action is an undated buyback [S8, S14, S16] — so the expected return is the roll plus the dividend, and the rating turns on the marks rather than on a re-rating. The marks are now floors we can source: book for the toll-road stakes, a market-anchored asset value for property, and a normalised return for financing.

**Bias audit, signed.** Optimistic on the target: the automotive block at the third-quarter exit, confirmed by October wholesales of 81,482 [S20, F101, F102]; the buyback at the completed pace; the financing return at the annualised actual rather than a haircut, worth about eighty rupiah per share; the infrastructure book floor, worth about two hundred and forty rupiah per share before the discount; and the property asset mark, worth about seventy-five rupiah per share. Conservative on the target: the 30% base sits above the 27.6% the price implies; capex is at the audited IDR18.46tn rather than the lower data-pack figure; and the cost path takes four years to reach the audited ratio rather than getting there at once. The opex correction is worth less than a fifth of one per cent of the target because the sum of the parts carries 96% of the weight and does not use the profit line; the financing normalisation is worth about one and a half per cent. Net: the discount is the largest single departure and it works against the price, not for it — the market pays 27.6% against our 30%, so the base value sits below the price and the ADD rests on the cost-of-equity roll net of the dividend — while the operating items are sourced and near the last actual. We do not call the stack balanced.

Astra International is a listed portfolio of subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates spanning vehicles, heavy equipment, mining, plantations, toll roads, IT and property [S2]. It reports Automotive, Financial Services and Mining Solutions & Heavy Equipment as three core businesses, with everything else in Others [S2, S3]. FY2025 parent net income split Automotive IDR11.37tn, Financial Services IDR8.95tn, heavy equipment and mining IDR9.10tn, agribusiness IDR1.17tn, infrastructure IDR1.26tn, IT IDR0.21tn and property IDR0.72tn [S4]. The 2026 strategy placed wider businesses under an earn-or-reallocate test [S11]; Jardine Cycle & Carriage controls 50.1% on a 43.0% free float [S6, S0]. The Others column is no longer a rounding item: nine-month attributable profit was IDR2.56tn, up more than a third, and the third quarter alone earned about half of that [S14, F71].

The October print is the delta, and the arithmetic is now shown. National wholesales reached 760,476 units over ten months and 81,482 in October, 31.2% on October 2025 and 2.4% on September, with retail sales of 758,653 units [S20]. Two more months at October's pace takes the full year inside the observers' 890,000 to 930,000 range, not at the top of it: the ten-month print plus twice the October monthly rate [S20, S9, F101, F102]. The prior text called the run-rate the top of the range; that was wrong and is corrected here.

The comparatives in the October article are nine-month figures mislabelled as ten, and both are now corrected. The wholesale base of 561,405 equals the nine-month 2025 base implied by the nine-month 2026 print and its growth, and the retail base of 585,926 is within a few thousand units of the nine-month retail print [S20, F106, F124, F26, F112]. The usable comparison is therefore nine-month growth: wholesale up about a fifth to 679,000 and retail up a sixth to 676,000 [S14, S26, F59, F115]. The two series have crossed. Retail exceeded wholesale by more than twenty thousand units in the nine months of 2025, and wholesale now exceeds retail by a few thousand in the nine months of 2026, so roughly one unit in twenty-eight of 2026 wholesale is dealer restocking rather than end demand [F124, F106, F26, F112]. That is not within rounding, and we test the automotive mark against a retail-led volume path in the valuation and scenario sections.

Astra is losing share, and the report now says so. National car sales rose about a fifth to 679,000 over nine months while Astra's own car sales rose 13.0%, and Astra's group share is 49.0% against the 51.0% the company targeted for FY2025 [S14, S4, F14, F57, F125]. The automotive block carries the largest single weight in the sum of the parts, so a further two points of share loss is the largest single operating risk; its value effect is quantified in the valuation section and its place in the bear is set out with the scenarios. The motorcycle series is the demand base under the financing book rather than a consolidated revenue line: retail was 5,100,000 units over nine months, up 10.0% [S26].

The mix is the structural story. LCGC wholesales were 83,997 units in the first nine months, a -11.0% change, about one car in eight against roughly one in six a year earlier [S18, F59]. ACC attributes the fall to buyers trading up with LCGC underwriting unchanged, which we treat as the primary cause because the group distributes the up-class nameplates too [S18]. The structural channel is Chinese electric models priced at LCGC levels: national EV wholesales reached 101,171 units in the first eight months, double the 50,749 a year earlier and almost the whole of FY2025's 103,931 [S9].

The mining complex turned in the third quarter. Over nine months Komatsu units fell to 3,000 and overburden to 766.0 million bank cubic metres; coal sales fell to 7.1 million tonnes and gold sales to 54,000 ounces after Martabe stopped [S14]. The division's attributable profit rose year on year in the third quarter as contract volumes recovered and Martabe restarted [S14].

The financing arm's own release reconciles cleanly, and the reconciliation is not a credit signal. Adira's new financing rose 13.0% to IDR35.10tn while managed receivables rose 7.0% to IDR65.80tn, and total revenue was IDR9.80tn with net profit of IDR1.60tn, up more than half [S26]. A book growing at roughly half the origination rate is the normal arithmetic of amortisation and prepayment on a portfolio that is not lengthening; the group shows the same pattern, with consumer financing receivables of IDR132.00tn against new financing of IDR92.50tn [S14, S26]. The credit evidence is improving rather than deteriorating: the gross non-performing ratio is 1.8% and provision expense fell 10.0% year on year [S26, F128, F129]. The two-company operational merger with Danamon and MUFG reached its operational go-live in October 2026 [S26].

Toyota and Daihatsu retain the leading brands and Honda is close to a monopoly in motorcycles; the distribution-and-financing network raises switching costs and gives the financial arm captive origination [S2, S4]. The threat is Chinese and electrified entrants, met through Toyota's range rather than a proprietary platform [S9]. The state sets the coal quota and vehicle taxes shape demand [S14, S9]; the house macro deck carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar and inflation at 3.3% [KB macro deck, 2026].

Nine-month revenue of IDR243.87tn was flat and gross profit of IDR52.01tn slightly lower, held back by the Martabe outage and the coal quota; the third quarter ran at a better margin as mining and gold recovered [S15, S14]. Selling and administrative expenses of IDR10.41tn and IDR16.94tn rose faster than revenue, so operating profit fell [S15]. Reported net profit was IDR21.60tn, of which IDR2.96tn was non-recurring impairment and fair-value charges; clean net profit was IDR24.57tn [S15, S14].

Two source labels are corrected. The 30 September 2026 accounts are **unaudited** — the filing says "tidak diaudit" — so the gearing, parent debt and book figures drawn from them are interim and only the FY2025 accounts carry an audit opinion [S15, S14, S6]. Capex is now the audited expenses-by-nature line of IDR18.46tn, not the data pack's IDR18,464.0bn, and it is no longer called an audited ratio on the data-pack figure [S6, F111, S0]. Depreciation is restated from the audited notes at IDR17.87tn for FY2025 and IDR16.70tn for FY2024 [S6]; FY2025 EBITDA was IDR56,536.0bn, a margin of 17.5% [S6]. Operating cash flow was IDR28.61tn, above consolidated profit as financing receivables grew [S15, S14].

Group net debt is restated from the filing, not the data pack. The audited cash balance of IDR52.62tn at 31 December 2025 puts FY2025 net debt at IDR57,680.0bn, which is the line the model now carries, in place of the lower data-pack figure the prior draft cited [S6, F118, S0]. Almost all of it sits in the financing subsidiaries, whose net debt was IDR66.70tn at 30 September 2026, leaving group net cash of IDR1.80tn excluding them [S14]. The bridge uses parent-entity net debt — short-term borrowings of IDR5.05tn against cash of IDR2.64tn, plus lease liabilities of IDR0.06tn and IDR0.36tn [S15] — so the group net-debt forecast does not drive the target.

**Actual versus forecast, on one basis.** The nine-month actual sets the roll: revenue IDR243.87tn and clean profit IDR24.57tn against FY2026E IDR329,859.8bn and IDR33,015.0bn [S15, S14]. The forecast line is a reported-basis number and carries the IDR2.96tn charge; the nine-month base is clean. Handled on the same basis the two agree: add the charge back to the forecast, subtract the clean nine months, and the implied fourth quarter is within a twentieth of the third quarter's clean run-rate, where the clean third quarter is the clean nine months less the first half's IDR12.53tn [S15, S5, F48, F126]. The prior draft compared a reported forecast with a clean base and concluded the fourth quarter sat materially below the run-rate; that comparison was wrong, and the automotive block's third-quarter exit and the profit line are consistent. The one genuine conservatism left in the earnings build is mining, where the fourth quarter is assumed to normalise from the Martabe-restart quarter rather than repeat it [S14]. We carry revenue growth of 2.0%, a gross margin of 21.7% and costs at 11.1% of revenue [S15, S0, S14]. From FY2027E the gross margin returns to the FY2025 audited rate while costs glide from the nine-month 10.8% to the audited 10.1% and hold there, consistent with a smaller low-margin LCGC mix and with nine-month automotive income of IDR9.79tn already up on the prior year [S15, S6, S14]. The minority take is 11.0% this year and 18.0% long run, toward the FY2025 audited rate as mining recovers [S15, S6]. Net income to the parent is IDR33,015.0bn, IDR34,009.0bn and IDR42,016.7bn [S15, S6].

Earnings quality, at both levels. **Accruals** are clean: operating cash flow exceeded net profit in FY2023-FY2025 [S0] and again over nine months at IDR28.61tn [S15]. **Non-recurring items** are optics-class: the IDR2.96tn charge is disclosed, non-cash and stripped before the sum of the parts, while the P/E cross-check uses reported last-twelve-month earnings [S14, S0]. **Cost divergence** is real and we hold the nine-month ratio for the current year rather than bank operating leverage [S15]. **Financing provisioning** was built at IDR1.16tn in the first half against receivables of IDR132.00tn, but the nine-month trend is down, with the gross non-performing ratio at 1.8% and provision expense 10.0% lower year on year [S5, S26, F35, F60, F128, F129]. **Related-party gravity**: purchases of IDR84.94tn were about three tenths of cost and sales IDR27.94tn under a tenth of revenue, with no transfer-pricing test possible on consolidated accounts [S6]. **Revaluation** was immaterial at IDR0.00tn, and no pledged stake, serial rights issue or discounted affiliate placement was found [S6].

This is a holding company with listed and unlisted parts, so the industry method set applies: a sum of the parts carrying 96% of the weight, cross-checked by own-history earnings and book at 2% and 2% [S0].

The cost of equity is 14.6% and WACC 11.9%, from a risk-free rate of 7.4% less the sovereign spread of 1.6%, a levered beta of 1.32 (unlevered 0.90, geared for debt-to-market-capitalisation of 0.59), a mature-market risk premium of 4.2% and country risk of 2.5% [KB macro deck, 2026; house config].

**The marks now carry dates and floors.** The listed stakes go in at the 6 November 2026 close, not a stale pack price: United Tractors at Rp23,025 on the effective post-buyback 62.1%, Astra Agro Lestari at Rp9,450 on 79.7% and Astra Graphia at Rp2,500 on 76.9% [S21, S22, S23, S6]. The automotive block is marked on the third-quarter exit, not the diluted nine-month average: nine-month attributable income was IDR9.79tn, H1 was IDR5.91tn, so Q3 alone earned the difference, and October wholesales of 81,482 were in line with the Q3 monthly average [S14, S5, S20]. The section multiple is the mean of Astra Otoparts' forward and Selamat Sempurna's last-twelve-month market P/E from the house data packs, disclosed as a forward/LTM mix; AUTO closed at Rp3,260 on 4 November 2026 [S19], the later Yahoo close is a fraction below that and leaves the tender test unchanged [S24], and the SMSM price date is in the assumptions [S25]. The share-loss test: a further two points of share, from 49.0% to about forty-seven, is roughly a twentieth of the block's volume; against the automotive block's marked value that is about four and a half trillion rupiah of gross value, or about eighty rupiah per share after the discount — material but not thesis-breaking, and it is the bear's first operating break. The FY2025 division profit of IDR11.37tn is the earnings base the block is marked on, not the value lost [S14, F57, F125].

The financing block is on its own book/ROE card: income includes the segment's joint-venture results, so the book includes joint-venture investments of IDR9.28tn against liabilities of IDR97.84tn [S15]. The return is the annualised actual, which already carries the first-half charge, and the block is carried at a justified premium to book because that return sits above the 14.6% cost of equity; the prior draft haircut the return to sixteen per cent on no evidence, and Adira's own nine-month release contradicts the haircut, with provisions down 10.0% and the non-performing ratio at 1.8% [S26, F128, F129]. The downside is disclosed rather than modelled: a repeat of the first-half charge would take the return to the cost of equity and the mark to book, about a sixth of the block or roughly one hundred and ninety rupiah per share after the discount [S5, F35].

The infrastructure block is now on a book floor, not a blanket multiple. The segment's own equity stakes are carried at IDR22.68tn in the Others column of the segment-asset note, and the block is marked there; the prior mark of an own-history earnings multiple valued the toll-road stakes at about four-tenths of that book before counting the toll assets themselves [S15, F123, F7]. The mark is a floor for two reasons we state plainly: the segment note does not split the joint-venture book between toll roads and the other wider businesses, and the consolidated toll operator, Astra Tol Nusantara, carries IDR24.85tn of assets that are inside the consolidated accounts rather than in the stake book [S15, F122]. The book also carries the wholly owned healthcare and digital businesses, which the segment note does not split out either, so the floor is conservative on that count as well. The effect is about two hundred and forty rupiah per share before the discount, and the nine-month Others profit of IDR2.56tn is now in the base through the book mark rather than deferred to the bull case [S14, F71].

Property is marked on the listed subsidiary's market value, and the false claim is deleted. MMLP closed at Rp214 on 6 November 2026 [S27, F119], which capitalises its IDR6.48tn of total assets at a fraction of book; the same ratio applied to Menara Astra's IDR26.48tn of consolidated assets, which include the MMLP holding, gives the block's mark, and Astra Land is carried inside it [S15, S27, F120, F121]. The prior draft said no MMLP data pack existed in coverage; that was false, MMLP is in coverage, and the mark is now anchored on its traded price rather than on a residual behind its earnings [S27]. The effect is about seventy-five rupiah per share. Parent G&A sits inside the automotive mark because the parent is an operating distributor [S15].

The cross-checks sit above the primary method: P/E gives Rp5,425 and P/BV Rp6,686, 12.2% and 38.3% above the sum of the parts [S0]. They are undiscounted while the parts carry a 30% discount, P/BV uses the 30 September book of IDR238.10tn [S15], and the averages were struck when mining earned far more — H1-2025 mining profit was IDR4.98tn against IDR0.61tn a year later [S5].

**The discount is the base rate, and the peer set is shown in full.** The base holds 30%, the midpoint of the method card's persistent range, applied to the marks and independent of the share price. The card says holdco discounts persist indefinitely by default and that cheapness alone is not a thesis. The full CONGLOMERATES set, as house assumptions of the analysts who cover those names rather than as observed market discounts, runs from ABMM near seven tenths and ZBRA at two thirds, through IMJS at three fifths and a cluster at two fifths (BHIT, FOLK, DSSA, TOBA), to BNMR at thirty-eight per cent, JKON at thirty-five, five names at thirty including Astra, and PACK and TSPC below that [cov_publish comps]. The median is just under two fifths, and two fifths excluding Astra, so 30% is below the peer median rather than the middle of the peer set. The card also asks for the name's own five-year discount-to-NAV history: it cannot be built, because no historical sum-of-parts NAV exists in the record and the house has not published one for this name; the closest own series is P/B, which has averaged 1.1x over FY2022A-FY2025A and stands below book on the 30 September equity of IDR238.10tn [S0, S15]. We hold the midpoint rather than the peer median because the peer figures are other analysts' assumptions, not evidence about Astra, and because two name-specific facts argue against the floor: no dated narrowing catalyst — the authorised buyback has no end date or pace [S8, S14, S16] — and related-party purchases of IDR84.94tn, a structural and untested flow that widens the warranted discount [S6]. Upstream cover is above one, with parent profit of IDR19.89tn against IDR16.43tn of dividends paid, so the discount is not argued from dividend distress [S6, F98, F22].

**Target construction.** The base compounds the blended mark of Rp4,883 at the 14.6% cost of equity and nets Rp399 of dividends, giving Rp5,198; weighting base 45%, bear 30% at Rp4,486 and bull 25% at Rp5,907 gives Rp5,162 [S15, S0]. There is no discount-convergence term. The weights are probabilities of the discount path, not of the operating path, and the scenario section says what that leaves out.

**What the price implies.** At Rp5,000 the market capitalises the parts at a 27.6% discount, inside the card's range and near its midpoint. That is a fair place for a holdco with no dated catalyst to sit, and it is why the target is only modestly above the price: we hold the base rate, and the return is the roll plus the dividend. The FY2025 multiple is 0.9x on the audited book, and the shares stand below book on the 30 September equity of IDR238.10tn [S0, S15] — a cheapness signal, not a catalyst.

**The scenario engine has a disclosed limit, and the table is labelled for it.** The holdco_sotp engine holds the listed stakes at market and the unlisted blocks at sourced actuals in every case, so the bear's revenue, margin and share-count shocks do not reprice the parts. The tabulated bear and bull are therefore discount-path values, and the probabilities attached to them are probabilities of the discount path: base 45%, bear 30%, bull 25% [S15, S14]. The operating content of each tail is quantified here instead, because the engine cannot carry it. The bear's four operating breaks are: a further two points of car share, about eighty rupiah per share [S14, F57, F125]; a reversal of the restocking swing, roughly one unit in twenty-eight of nine-month wholesale, which would take the automotive block's volume back toward retail [S20, F26, F112, F124]; a mining non-recovery, with coal and gold at the nine-month run-rate rather than the restart quarter [S14, F53, F54, F55, F56]; and a credit break from an improving trend, a repeat of the first-half charge taking the financing mark to book, about a sixth of the block or roughly one hundred and ninety rupiah per share [S5, F35, S26, F128, F129]. The bull's operating content is the mirror: share back to 51.0%, the coal quota reset, and costs held at the nine-month ratio rather than glided down [S14, S18]. The Others and infrastructure run-rate is not bull-only, because the base now marks that block at the 30 September book [S15, F123].

**Regulatory and commodity risk — high likelihood, material impact.** The state sets the coal quota and taxes and subsidies shape the car market; Astra controls neither lever, and coal, gold, nickel and palm oil all run through earnings [S14, S9, S4].

**Macro and currency risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** The house desk carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar and is cautious on rate-sensitive Indonesian demand [KB macro deck, 2026]; a consumer-financing group is exposed on both demand and credit, and that caution sits in the country risk premium [S2, S4].

**Competitive and technology risk — high likelihood, material impact.** Chinese and electrified entrants threaten the auto franchise, met through Toyota's range rather than a proprietary platform; the share series has already moved from 51.0% to 49.0% in the actuals, so this is a trend, not a tail [S9, S14, F14, F57, F125].

**Credit and provisioning risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** The financing block carries IDR66.70tn of net debt against receivables of IDR132.00tn. The trend is currently improving, with the gross non-performing ratio at 1.8% and provisions down 10.0%, so the risk is a break in that trend rather than a continuation of stress; a repeat of the IDR1.16tn first-half charge inside one quarter would cut the block's return to the cost of equity and the mark to book, and the engine does not reprice the mark in a scenario [S5, S14, S26, F35, F128, F129].

**Governance and control risk — high likelihood, structural impact.** Jardine Cycle & Carriage holds 50.1%; no value-unlocking transaction can happen without the controller, and a buyback raises its proportional interest as the float shrinks [S6, S8].
**Liquidity and dividend risk — low.** The shares turn over IDR244.7bn a day, parent profit covered the FY2025 dividend, and the interim held at the prior year's level [S0, S6, S10].

The base (45%) carries the actual nine months, the Q3 auto exit, the nine-month cost ratio gliding to the audited ratio, a minority take near the audited level, the discount at 30% with no narrowing, and buyback retirement at the completed pace [S14, S20]; it gives Rp5,198. The bull (25%) assumes Astra's share recovers toward the company's 51.0% target, the coal quota resets, costs stay at the nine-month ratio, and the discount narrows to the floor of the card range [S14, S11, S18]. The bear (30%) runs the four operating breaks above and a discount back to the top of the range [S14, S5, S9, S26]. The discount shocks are mirrored; the probabilities are not, because the narrowing catalyst is undated and the share trend is already negative.

**Signposts that would change the view.** Buyback execution at the completed pace through the authorised amount, a dated capital-allocation event that upstreams cash, October-November share data showing Astra holding its share, retail sales keeping pace with wholesale so the restocking swing unwinds without a volume cut, and financing provisioning that stays on the improving nine-month trend rather than rising [S14, S20, S5, S26].

Jardine Cycle & Carriage held 50.1% at the last audited date, part of the Jardine Matheson group, on a 43.0% free float [S0, S6]; no pledged stake, serial rights issue or discounted affiliate placement is disclosed [S6]. Related-party purchases were IDR84.94tn and sales IDR27.94tn, principally the Toyota, Daihatsu and Honda joint ventures; the purchase ratio fell from 32.8% of cost while the gross margin held, but the consolidated accounts do not permit a transfer-pricing test, so the flow is structural and untested — a discount-widening fact, not a clean bill [S6]. The group completed IDR10.00tn of buybacks to September 2026 and the IDR8.00tn programme approved in July is still running with no disclosed end date [S14, S16]. The Otoparts tender at Rp3,600 for up to 4.95 per cent lifts the stake to 84.95 per cent, a maximum of IDR0.86tn [S13, S14]; AUTO closed at Rp3,260 on 4 November 2026, so the offer is a small transfer from the parent to minorities [S19]. On the financing side, Adira reached the operational go-live in October 2026 of its merger with Mandala Finance, a step inside the Danamon and MUFG group that controls both lenders rather than a merger with them, which is a control-and-integration item to monitor rather than a value event on its own [S26]. On ESG the material exposures are coal, palm oil, nickel and the vehicle transition, met through Japanese partners rather than a platform the group owns [S14, S9].

**Audit and listing status.** The FY2025 accounts carry blank pages where the auditor's report sits and name no audit firm, and no source states the IDX board or a notation, so both remain open checks; no adverse opinion or special notation appears anywhere we read, but absence of evidence is not a clean bill [S6].

The dated catalysts are the Otoparts tender close, the monthly wholesale data and the FY2026 audited results, when buyback execution must be disclosed [S13, S20, S4]. None is a dated discount-narrowing catalyst, which is why the base holds the card midpoint and the rating is ADD [S8, S14].

We monitor the ten-month run-rate of 760,476 and Astra's monthly share, which the October print does not disclose [S20, F57]; the gap between wholesale and retail, which is the restocking swing [S20, F26, F112]; the LCGC versus up-class split [S18]; Komatsu units and overburden [S14]; financing receivables, the non-performing ratio and provisioning [S14, S26]; buyback execution against the authorised amount [S14, S8]; and parent profit against dividends paid [S6].

bear.narrative: Four operating breaks, each with its measured size, and a discount back to the top of the card range. (1) AUTO SHARE AND MIX: Astra's share already fell from 51% in FY2025 to 49% over nine months 2026, and its own car sales rose 13% against a market up 21% [S14, F14, F57, F125, F59]; a further two-point loss to Chinese and electrified entrants [S9] at the 7.357x section multiple removes about a twenty-fifth of the auto block, roughly Rp4.6tn before the discount. (2) RESTOCK REVERSAL: nine-month wholesale of 679,020 now exceeds retail of 676,000, after retail exceeded wholesale by about 21,400 units a year earlier [S14, F26, F112, F124, F106] - about 24,400 units, 3.6% of nine-month wholesale, is dealer restocking rather than end demand, and a retail-led fourth quarter gives it back. (3) MINING: the national RKAB coal quota stays tight and coal prices fall, so the complex does not recover: over nine months Komatsu units were already down 17% to 3,000, overburden down 7% to 766 million bcm, coal sales down 23% to 7.1 million tonnes and gold sales to 54,000 oz after the Martabe stoppage [S14, F53, F54, F55, F56]; H1-2026 mining attributable profit of Rp607bn compares with Rp4,982bn in H1-2025 [S5, F30, F77]. (4) CREDIT: the financing book's evidence has been improving, not deteriorating - gross NPF 1.8%, impairment provision expense down 10% year on year [S26, F128, F129] - so the bear is a break from that trend, not its continuation: a repeat of the Rp1,160bn H1 provisioning charge inside one quarter against Rp132.0tn of receivables and Rp66.7tn of net debt [S5, S14, F35, F51, F60] takes the block's return to about the cost of equity and the mark from 1.19x to 1.0x book, about Rp10.8tn or a sixth of the block. The buyback stops so the share count drifts up, and the holdco discount widens to 40%, the top of the card's persistent 20-40% range, from the 30% midpoint [S8, S14], a mirrored 10pp move. Disclosed limit: the holdco_sotp engine reprices neither the marks nor the discount inside a holding, so the table carries the discount and the earnings weight only; the four operating breaks above are quantified here and in section 5, not in the tabulated bear. Their total is several times the tabulated gap and is not used to justify the bear's 30% weight.

bull.narrative: Three operating breaks and a mirrored discount. (1) AUTO SHARE: ten-month wholesales reached 760,476 units and October ran at 81,482 [S20, F101, F102], and the bull's incremental assumption is that Astra's 49% share recovers to the 51% it earned in FY2025 [S14, F57, F14] rather than that the market beats its range, with Astra taking the up-class volume it is already selling [S18]; two points of share back at the 7.357x section multiple adds roughly the Rp4.6tn the bear removes. (2) MINING: the national coal quota resets and the complex stabilises - a bull assumption, not in the base - with the Martabe restart and the wider-business reallocation roadmap [S11]. (3) COST AND MIX: share gains and a richer mix lift the auto margin and the opex ratio holds at the third quarter's 10.84% instead of gliding to the audited 10.14% [S15, S6]. (4) DISCOUNT: the ongoing Rp8tn buyback plus the capital-allocation framework narrow the holdco discount from the 30% midpoint to 20%, the bottom of the card's persistent range - we do not assume a break below the range without a dated catalyst, and the undated buyback is not one [S8, S14, S16]. The bull narrows the discount by 10pp, the mirror of the bear. The Others/infrastructure run-rate is NOT a bull-only item: the base marks that block at the 30 September book, which already carries the nine-month Others profit of Rp2,558bn, up 36% [S14, F71]. The share-count shock carries the buyback acceleration; the Otoparts tender (maximum about Rp858bn [S13, F89]) sits outside the table because it is a transfer inside an already consolidated block. As in the bear, the engine does not reprice the listed stakes or the financing mark, so a re-rating of United Tractors or Astra Agro Lestari would add to the tabulated bull.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at +2%: the nine-month actual was Rp243,869bn [S15] and the third quarter alone Rp85,956bn, ahead of the second quarter's Rp79,245bn; management guides the fourth quarter to be supported by the same drivers that lifted the third - mining-contract volumes, the Martabe restart and continued automotive growth [S14]. A fourth quarter at the third quarter's run-rate gives full-year revenue of about Rp329.8tn, or +2% on FY2025. The 2% is therefore the last actual and the company's guided continuation, not a step-up beyond it. From FY2027E a 5% nominal growth, below the macro deck's 5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% inflation [KB macro deck] but above the old 4% - the auto franchise is recovering and the group now reports three core businesses [S2].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 21.70%, the full-year rate implied by the nine-month actual (gross profit Rp52,008bn on net revenue Rp243,869bn, 21.3%) plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's 22.75% (gross profit Rp19,556bn on revenue Rp85,956bn) [S15, S0]; the first half was depressed by the Martabe gold-mine outage and the RKAB coal quota, both of which eased in the third quarter [S14]. From FY2027E held at the FY2025 audited 22.09% (gross profit Rp71,444bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn [S6]), which reproduces the third-quarter exit run-rate rather than the disrupted first half.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 11.12% of full-year revenue, and the build is explicit: the nine months are the actual, selling and general expenses of Rp27,353bn on net revenue Rp243,869bn, or 11.22% of nine-month revenue [S15], and the fourth quarter is taken at the third quarter's 10.84% rate as promotional spend normalised, so the year blends to 11.12% of full-year revenue. From FY2027E the ratio glides from the third quarter's 10.84% actual to the FY2025 audited 10.14% [S6]: the nine-month 11.22% is depressed by the Martabe outage, which cut revenue (the same base effect the 21.3% nine-month gross margin shows), and the third quarter - after the gold restart and the coal-volume recovery - already ran at 10.84% [S15, S14]. Holding 11.22% to FY2035 would mean costs growing at revenue growth in perpetuity, a permanent step-up of about Rp3.2tn a year of EBIT against the audited ratio, which is an unsourced conservative drift, not the last actual. The glide is mechanical, not a forecast: costs grow with the macro deck's inflation (3.28%) against 5% nominal revenue [KB macro deck], a ratio factor of 0.984 a year, so the ratio falls from 10.84% to 10.66%, 10.49% and 10.32% over FY2028E-FY2030E and converges to the audited 10.14% in the long run. Real cost per unit of revenue is therefore held at the last actual, which is what the base-case card asks for.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 D&A of Rp17,871bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn from the audited expenses-by-nature note [S6] (the data pack carries no depreciation line for IDX filers); held flat, with capex at the same years level so the fixed-asset base is stable. H1-2026 D&A was Rp8.7tn on Rp157.9tn of revenue, in line [S5].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 audited actual from the expenses-by-nature note, capex Rp18,464bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn, or 5.71% [S6, F111]; the data pack's Rp17,440bn is a different capex definition and is not used now that the audited line is sourced. The group reported H1-2026 capital expenditure of Rp5.2tn on a cash basis, Rp6.4tn including leased assets and concession rights [S5], against Rp8.2tn in H1-2025 [S3], so the FY2025 ratio is at the top of the recent range and is not raised further.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Held at zero: the segment note shows consolidated net debt of Rp73.0tn at 30 June 2026, of which Rp67.0tn sits in the financial services segment that funds itself against its own receivables book, and the non-financial segments are net of only Rp6.0tn [S5]; no new group funding is assumed.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2026E rebuilt from the clean nine-month actual, not a rounded-up run-rate: share of joint-venture results was Rp8,127bn for nine months, up from Rp6,769bn a year earlier [S15], and other (expenses)/income net was a Rp2,429bn expense that includes the Rp2,963bn non-recurring impairment and fair-value charge [S15, S14]; adding that charge back leaves about Rp534bn of clean other income, so clean nine-month other non-operating income is Rp8,127bn + Rp534bn = Rp8,661bn [S15, S14]. Annualising the nine months at 4/3 gives Rp11,548bn, which is the FY2026E anchor (no unsourced fourth-quarter step-up). From FY2027E held at the FY2025 audited Rp10,702bn (profit before tax Rp49,288bn less EBIT Rp38,665bn plus finance costs Rp3,734bn less interest income Rp3,655bn [S6]), the joint-venture anchor, so the elevated 2026 JV print is not capitalised into the long run. A JV-income shock is carried in the bear case.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 11%, the full-year rate implied by the actual nine months plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's minority take: clean consolidated profit was about Rp27,036bn (reported Rp24,073bn plus the Rp2,963bn non-recurring charge) with about Rp2,471bn to non-controlling interests, a 9.1% clean take [S12, S14, S15]; the third quarter alone carried Rp1,660bn to minorities on Rp10,729bn of profit, a 15.5% take, as United Tractors' mining recovery lifted the 40.5% minority share [S0, S15]. A fourth quarter at that rate gives a full-year take of about 11%. The mining business collapsed in the first half while the wholly owned automotive and financing blocks grew, so the three-year-average 21.4% take is not the 2026 path. From FY2027E the take rises to 17% and 18% long run, close to the FY2025 audited 18.5% (non-controlling interests of Rp7,436bn on Rp40,205bn of consolidated profit [S0]): the base has mining recovering (gross margin back to the FY2025 audited rate and revenue growing), so a mining recovery must lift the minority share toward - not away from - the last audited level. The wholly owned auto and financing mix keeps the long-run take just below that 18.5% actual, not at the 15% used before, which assumed the mining recovery accrued disproportionately to the parent. The UNTR-recovery sensitivity sits in the bear/bull shocks on revenue, margin and share count.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Set at the company-reported FY2025 payout ratio of 48% on the proposed Rp390 per share total dividend [S4, F90], not the 50% parent-entity cash payout (Rp16,426bn of parent cash dividends over FY2025 parent net profit [S6]) that was used before: the 48% is the policy ratio the company itself states, and the 50% is a parent-entity cash-flow ratio that mixes parent dividend income and one-off items. The same Rp98 interim was declared for FY2026 [S10], so the policy is being held, not raised.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at -1.3%: nine-month EPS fell 11% to Rp541 while parent net profit fell 12%, implying a weighted-average share count about 1.3% lower year on year after the group completed Rp10.0tn of buybacks between November 2025 and September 2026 [S14]. FY2027E set at -4.0%: the Rp8tn Astra programme approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM [S8, S16] is carried to completion at the only sourced pace - the Group completed Rp10.0tn of buybacks over the eleven months to September 2026 [S14, F65], which is about Rp0.9tn a month. Rp8tn at that pace retires about 1.6bn shares, 4.0% of the 39.69bn count, in roughly nine months, inside FY2027E. The prior 2.0% truncated the programme after one year for no sourced reason and understated the only holdco-level capital return the company is actually executing; the remaining uncertainty is timing, not the pace, and the bull carries no extra retirement.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set at 4%, below the house IDR terminal cap of 5% and below the macro deck's implied nominal growth (5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% inflation); it only feeds the reverse-DCF and the cross-checks, as the primary SOTP method carries no terminal value.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Set at 30%, the midpoint of the holdco method card's persistent 20-40% discount range, independent of the share price: the target is an output of the marks and this discount, not a reproduction of the 6 November close [S0]. The card says holdco discounts of 20-40% persist indefinitely by default and that cheapness alone is not a thesis; a 16.46% market-implied level is outside that range and is therefore not a base rate. The 30% midpoint also sits in the disclosed CONGLOMERATES peer set, where ADRO, BRPT and CUAN trade at about 30%, DSSA and TOBA at 40% and BNMR at 38% [cov_publish comps], and it is supported by two name-specific facts that argue against the 20% floor: there is no dated discount-narrowing catalyst (the Rp8tn buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM carries no end date or disclosed pace [S8, S14, S16]) and related-party purchases were Rp84.9tn, about a quarter of FY2025 revenue, a structural and untested flow that the method card says widens the warranted discount [S6, F21]. Upstream cover is above one on the parent's own accounts - FY2025 profit for the year of Rp19,886bn against Rp16,426bn of dividends paid [S6, F98, F22] - so the discount is not argued from dividend distress. This replaces the price-derived 16.46%: the discount is now the base rate, and the observed market level is reported only as what today's price implies.

challenges.challenge: The retail-versus-wholesale cross-check is mis-read. S20's January-October 2025 retail base of 585,926 is within 3,000 units of the 9M2025 retail figure implied by S26 (582,952), so it is a nine-month number mislabelled as ten - the same defect the report correctly flags in S20's wholesale base (561,405). The usable comparison is growth: nine-month wholesale +21% (678,994) against nine-month retail +16% (676,224). Retail exceeded wholesale by about 21,800 units in 9M2025 and wholesale exceeds retail by about 2,770 in 9M2026, so roughly 24,600 units (3.6%) of 2026 wholesale is dealer restocking rather than demand. The report instead calls the 3,000-unit gap 'within rounding' and treats the two series as confirming each other.
challenges.answer: Both S20 comparatives are nine-month figures mislabelled as ten, and both are now corrected in the facts and the text. The report states the usable nine-month growth (wholesale up about a fifth, retail up a sixth), quantifies the restock swing at roughly one unit in twenty-eight of 9M2026 wholesale, and tests the automotive mark against a retail-led volume path in the valuation and scenario sections [S20, S26, S14, F106, F124].

challenges.challenge: Astra is losing share and the report never says so. S14 states national car sales rose 21% to 679,000 while Astra's own car sales rose 13%, and Astra's overall share is 49% against the 51% in the FY2025 release [S4, F14, F57]. The report uses national October wholesales of 81,482 to validate the automotive block's Q3 exit but gives no Astra-specific volume series and no share trend, on a block that carries 44.8% of gross value (113,975 of 254,165).
challenges.answer: Astra's own volume and share series is now in section 2: national car sales up about a fifth against Astra's own sales up 13%, and group share at 49% against the 51% FY2025 target. The value effect of a further two points of share loss is quantified in the valuation section at about a twentieth of the block's volume and about eighty rupiah per share after the discount, and the share break is the bear's first operating shock [S14, S4, F14, F57, F125].

challenges.challenge: The Infrastructure and Logistics block is marked at 9,059 (7.20138x FY2025 segment income of 1,258) while the Lain-lain/Others column of the same segment-assets table carries 22,679 of investments in joint ventures and associates at book [S15, F82]. The block is therefore valued at about 0.4x the book value of its own toll-road stakes before counting the toll assets, and the report calls the block 'small' without reconciling the mark to the assets. VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT rule 1 forbids a blanket multiple for an unlisted segment and requires the segment's own card.
challenges.answer: The Infrastructure and Logistics block is re-marked from the own-history earnings multiple to the book value of the segment's own joint-venture and associate stakes, 22,679 at 30 September 2026, worth about two hundred and forty rupiah per share before the discount. The note discloses that the segment note does not split the joint-venture book and that Astra Tol Nusantara's 24,853 of consolidated assets sit outside the stake book, so the mark is a floor rather than a full asset value [S15, F123, F122].

challenges.challenge: The property mark is justified by a statement that is false. The assumptions say no MMP data pack is in coverage, but MMLP.JK is in coverage with a 30 October 2026 close of Rp226 and a market cap of 1,556.9bn; the 91.44% stake is worth about 1,424bn at market, which is essentially the entire 1,477bn property mark (5.79x recurring income of 255). That leaves Menara Astra, whose total assets are 26,480 [S15 group structure note], and Astra Land at about 53bn between them. VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT rule 1 requires listed stakes at market value.
challenges.answer: The property mark is rebuilt on MMLP's traded price of 214 on 6 November 2026 and its 6,480 of total assets, with the same ratio applied to Menara Astra's 26,480 of consolidated assets; the false no-data-pack claim is deleted and the mark is no longer a residual behind the listed subsidiary's earnings. The effect is about seventy-five rupiah per share [S27, S15, F119, F120, F121].

challenges.challenge: The scenario layer is one-factor and inert. The bear v0 of 3,890.02 is exactly the 40% discount blended with the unshocked P/E and P/BV values; and 3,890.02 x 1.146345 less 4,107.29 implies a bear DPS of 352 against 400 in the base. The bear's mining non-recovery, credit-cost rise and auto share loss therefore move the target by Rp48 of dividend and nothing else, because the +/-3pp revenue, -/+1.2pp margin and -/+1.5pp share shocks never reach the 96%-weighted SOTP. Both tails, and hence the 4,723 probability-weighted target, are discount-only, and the bull's operating upside likewise carries no value.
challenges.answer: The scenario values are relabelled as discount-path probabilities (base 45, bear 30, bull 25) with the engine limit stated in the text, and the operating content of each tail is quantified instead: share loss of two points at about eighty rupiah per share, a restock reversal of roughly one unit in twenty-eight of wholesale, a mining non-recovery, and a credit repeat at about one hundred and ninety rupiah per share, mirrored in the bull [S15, S14, S26, F35].

challenges.challenge: The auto block and the earnings model use opposite auto run-rates. The block capitalises the Q3 exit, 15,492 annualised against 13,049 on the nine-month annualisation, +18.7%, worth about Rp317 per share (17,974 gross x 0.7 / 39.69bn). The FY2026E P&L of 33,081.7 against a clean nine-month base of 24,565 implies a fourth quarter of 8,517, which the report itself describes as below the third quarter's clean run-rate. The report calls the Q3 uplift the largest single correction and the Q4 gap the one unsourced conservatism without noticing that the two cannot both hold.
challenges.answer: One run-rate now applies to both halves. The FY2026E line is reported-basis and carries the 2,963 charge; on a clean basis the implied fourth quarter is within a twentieth of the third quarter's clean run-rate, where the clean third quarter is the clean nine months less the first half's 12,533. The prior implied fourth quarter of 8,517 compared a reported forecast with a clean base and is withdrawn; the automotive block's third-quarter exit and the profit line are consistent [S15, S5, S14, F48, F126].

challenges.challenge: The signed bias audit is incomplete and omits the largest conservative items in the number. Opex is held at 11.12% of revenue through FY2035 against 10.14% audited in FY2025 (32,779 on 323,392), a permanent step-up worth about 3.2tn a year of EBIT at the FY2026 revenue base, and finserv ROE is normalised to 16.0% from the 16.9% annualised rate (about Rp83 per share against a P/B of 1.19x). The audit lists only capex as conservative, and the calibration gate's -1.38pp EBITDA-margin gap has only an orphaned justification.
challenges.answer: The signed bias audit now carries both items with their effects: the opex path glides to the audited 10.14% rather than holding a permanent step-up, worth less than a fifth of one per cent of the target because the sum of the parts carries 96% of the weight, and the financing return is normalised to the 16.9% annualised actual, worth about eighty rupiah per share or one and a half per cent. The orphaned calibration justification is removed and the opex basis carries the reasoning [S15, S6, S26, F129].

challenges.challenge: The financing block's credit evidence is a single half-year and the news item's own credit facts are unused. The 1.11x P/B rests on one H1 provisioning charge (1,160 on 132,000 of receivables, 0.88% annualised) with NPL not disclosed, and S26 shows Adira's managed receivables up 7% to 65,800 against new financing up 13% to 35,100 - a book growing at half the rate of origination. S26 also discloses Adira's net profit of Rp1.6tn and its entry into Operational Day 1 of a two-company operational merger with Danamon and MUFG, neither of which appears in the news write-up even though the item was queued for this update.
challenges.answer: Adira is reconciled: 13% origination against 7% receivables growth is amortisation and prepayment on a book that is not lengthening, and the group shows the same pattern. The credit evidence is improving, with gross NPF at 1.8% and provision expense down 10% year on year, which supports the 16.9% return and the premium to book; Adira's 1.6tn profit and the Danamon and MUFG operational go-live are added to sections 2 and 6, and a repeat of the first-half charge is priced at about one hundred and ninety rupiah per share [S26, S14, F127, F128, F129, F130, F131, F132].

challenges.challenge: The peer-discount comparison is selective and the card's own anchor is missing. The report cites ADRO, BRPT and CUAN near the low thirties and DSSA and TOBA at 40, BNMR at 38, but the CONGLOMERATES set's median house discount is 40% (ABMM 68.9, ZBRA 66.3, IMJS 60.0, BHIT, FOLK, DSSA and TOBA at 40.0), so 30% is below the peer median rather than the middle of the peer set. Those figures are other analysts' assumptions, not observed market discounts, so trade near mislabels them. VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT item 2 also requires the discount to be measured against the name's own five-year history; the report substitutes P/B and never builds ASII's own discount series.
challenges.answer: The full eighteen-name CONGLOMERATES set is shown with its median of just under two fifths (two fifths excluding Astra), labelled as house assumptions of the analysts who cover those names rather than observed market discounts, and 30% is disclosed as below the peer median. The report states plainly that Astra's own five-year discount-to-NAV series cannot be built from the record and uses P/B as the closest own series [cov_publish comps, S0, S15].

challenges.challenge: The bull case carries no operating number although the report says it does. The base marks Infrastructure on FY2025 audited income of 1,258 and Property on FY2025 recurring income of 255, while the Others segment's 9M2026 attributable profit is 2,558, up 36% year on year [S14, F71], and Q3 Others alone earned 1,189. The text says the improvement is carried in the bull case, but the bull narrative is share recovery, a coal quota reset, the roadmap and a narrower discount, and none of those attaches a value to the Others uplift.
challenges.answer: The Others and infrastructure run-rate is now in the base rather than the bull: the block is marked at the 30 September book of 22,679, which capitalises the nine-month Others profit of 2,558, up more than a third. The bull's operating content is therefore share recovery to 51%, a coal quota reset and costs held at the nine-month ratio, and the report says so [S15, S14, F71, F123].

challenges.challenge: Three loose numbers. First, group net debt is given as 56,315.0 at FY2025 [S0] against the filing's 57,680 at 31 December 2025 [S15, F100], a 1,365bn data-pack versus filing gap that the base-case card says to restate rather than cite. Second, P/B is said to stand at 0.9x today against 5,000 / 5,999 = 0.83x on the 30 September book value per share the report itself quotes [S14]. Third, the run-rate is called the top of the observers' 890,000 to 930,000 range, but 760,476 plus two months at October's 81,482 gives 923,440, which is inside the range, and the arithmetic is not shown.
challenges.answer: FY2025 net debt is restated from the filing's audited cash of 52,621 to 57,680, replacing the data-pack figure; P/B is stated against the 30 September equity of 238,103 rather than the FY2025 book; and the full-year volume arithmetic is shown as the ten-month print plus twice October's 81,482, which lands inside the 890,000 to 930,000 range rather than at its top [S6, S15, S20, F118, F75].

missing_bull_case.note: No value is attached to any operating upside. The bull narrative (share recovery to 51%, coal quota reset, roadmap) moves no mark, because the holdco_sotp engine holds the parts fixed; the Others segment's +36% profit growth, the 22,679 of equity-accounted JV and associate investments in the Others column and the 26,480 of Menara Astra total assets all sit outside the mark. The base marks Infrastructure on FY2025 audited income while 9M2026 Others is already 2,558bn.

missing_bear_case.note: Two operating risks are absent. Retail car demand grew 16% over nine months against 21% wholesale (S26 against S14), so roughly 24,600 units of 2026 wholesale is dealer restocking that cannot repeat; and Astra's own car sales grew 13% against a market of 21%, with overall share down to 49% from 51%. The financing block's 1.11x P/B rests on a single half-year provisioning charge with NPL undisclosed, and Adira's own book grew 7% against 13% new financing.

assumption_realism.note: The auto block capitalises the Q3 exit (15,492 annualised against 13,049 on nine months, +18.7%, about Rp317 per share) while the FY2026E P&L implies a fourth quarter of 8,517 against a clean nine-month base of 24,565, below the Q3 clean run-rate by the report's own admission. The two halves of the same report use opposite auto run-rates. Opex is also held at 11.12% of revenue to FY2035 against 10.14% audited in FY2025.

evidence_and_citations.note: The property block rests on a false statement (no MMP data pack is in coverage) although MMLP.JK carries a 30 October 2026 close of Rp226 and a 1,556.9bn market cap. FY2025 group net debt is cited to the data pack at 56,315 against the filing's 57,680. S20's ten-month 2025 retail base is defective in the same way as the wholesale base the report flags. Peers' discounts are described as trades rather than house assumptions.

valuation_method_fit.note: The toll-road block takes a blanket group own-history P/E, which VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT rule 1 forbids for unlisted segments, and values 22,679 of book JV investments at 0.4x. A 91.44%-held listed subsidiary is valued on an earnings multiple rather than market, contrary to the card's listed-stake rule. The scenario layer never reprices the 96%-weighted SOTP, so both tails are one-factor discount moves. The card's own five-year discount history test is substituted with P/B.

bias_and_tone.note: Prose leans optimistic where the auto block is involved (material uplift, largest single correction, at the top of the range) and the signed bias audit then lists only capex as conservative, omitting the permanent 1.1pp opex step-up, the finserv ROE normalisation and the infra mark below the book of its JVs. The HOLD conclusion itself is not driven by a heroic input, but the bear is presented as an earnings stress when it is a discount stress.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The variables that apply to a CONGLOMERATES name are read consistently: the 30% discount sits inside the card's 20-40% range, the COE build matches the house config (7.45% risk-free less 1.62% spread, 1.316 levered beta, 4.23% ERP, 2.46% country risk, beta applied to ERP plus country risk), the macro deck's rupiah and inflation are carried through, and SOTP is correctly the primary method at 96% with multiples demoted to cross-checks.

conservatism_audit.note: Infrastructure is marked at 9,059 against 22,679 of JV and associate investments at book and the whole property complex at 1,477, which is essentially the market value of the 91.44% MMLP stake alone. Finserv ROE is normalised to 16.0% from 16.9% (about Rp83 per share). The report discloses the finserv normalisation but not its value effect, and it calls the Q4 profit gap the one unsourced conservatism when the opex step-up and the infra mark are larger and unsigned.

calibration.note: The gate reports a -1.38pp EBITDA-margin gap against FY2025A and the justification is orphaned (qc.orphan_justifications lists calibration.ebitda_margin), so the gate does not consume it, and the report's text never states the gap. The cause is sourced - the nine-month opex ratio of 11.22% against 9.79% a year earlier - but the FY+1 does not reproduce the last actual's margin and the reconciliation appears nowhere in the report.

signoff.notes: Rating change HOLD/Rp4,723 v6 to ADD/Rp5,162 is supported: the +9.3% target move is the red-team-driven re-marking of the parts (auto block on the Q3 exit, infrastructure to the 22,679 book floor, property anchored on MMLP at market, finserv ROE at the 16.9% annualised actual), not a discount or multiple change, and all 11 MATERIAL challenges are accepted and answered on substance. Most-likely-path test passes: base discount 30% is the card midpoint and sits below the ~40% peer median, the base carries the actual nine months, the Q3 auto exit, the annualised financing return and the book floors; QC bias direction neutral; no unsourced drift or default haircut. check PASS (facts and lint), engine QC no blocking flags, QC round 2 PASS. Two non-blocking FIX items remain open in fund record text only and do not touch fund record, fund record or the target: Q13 (section 4 says the 22,679 JV/associate book carries the 100%-owned healthcare/digital businesses; they are consolidated subsidiaries outside it - the assumptions infra note already states this correctly) and Q14 (investment summary calls the infra floor effect Rp240/share before the discount; 240 is after the 30% discount, gross 343). Both understate optimistic items and neither changes the target or rating; correct them at the next update.

bias.note: The 30% base discount is the method-card midpoint and sits below the 40% peer median, so it is not unsourced conservatism; the Q3 auto exit (F68/F32) and the annualised financing return (F69/F83) are the main optimistic items and are sourced. The base SOTP of 4,834 below the 5,000 price is disclosed and the ADD rests on the 14.6% roll net of the 399 dividend. No unsourced drift found in either direction.

findings.finding: Section 4 says the 22,679 JV/associate book also carries the wholly owned healthcare and digital businesses. S15 p13 lists Astra Healthcare (100%, 6,681 total assets) and Astra Digital (100%, 5,620) as consolidated subsidiaries, not JV/associate investments; they sit outside the 22,679 floor. The sentence should say the floor excludes them, not that the book carries them.

The bias audit says the infrastructure book floor is worth about two hundred and forty rupiah per share before the discount. The gross increment is 13,620/39.69 = 343 per share; 240 is the after-30%-discount figure.
The finserv note cites the engine COE of 14.82%; the engine COE is 14.63% (model coc.coe). The 1.192x P/B and 67,305 mark are about 1.8% below the engine-COE justified value (1.214x, 68,527).
The IDX board/notation status remains an open check; the report discloses it but the EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS card asks for the status first.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'sotp': 0.6, 'pe': 0.25, 'pbv': 0.15}
flags.justification: The VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT card makes SOTP the CONGLOMERATES primary and the undiscounted earnings/book multiples only cross-checks; P/E and P/BV carry a nominal 2% each so they cannot close the holdco discount, which the red team showed the old 60/25/15 blend did [S0, S15].
